review_scope: Full 37-line article read. Public-only metadata and qualified private-repository body assertion conflict with general concept wording; scope remains unresolved. Feature declaration, product variables and linked MCP contracts need further review. No native behavior or privilege evidence.

claims.statement: Article product metadata describes public cloud repositories, narrower than the body assertion about certain private repositories.
Version applicability is delegated to the copilot feature definition rather than explicit version ranges in this article.
The introductory claim describes prevention of inadvertent credential exposure; it is not observed zero exposure or complete detection coverage.
The body describes secret blocking in AI-generated MCP responses, a distinct path from repository writes.
The body describes secret prevention in MCP actions, with issue creation as an example; this does not prove every tool or action is covered.
The body describes default protection for MCP interactions with public repositories independently of the repository push-protection setting.

The body additionally describes default protection for private repositories covered by GHAS independently of the repository push-protection setting; this qualified assertion conflicts with public-only general wording and needs authoritative scope verification.
The documented non-bypass block response removes the secret from request content before retry.
The article conditions visibility of the MCP bypass option on repository or personal-account push-protection enablement; default MCP protection is not equivalent to this bypass prerequisite.
The article asks users to evaluate safety before bypassing; UI availability is not an approved exception or independent evidence that inclusion is safe.
